whole_task_feasibility.question: Can the current system learn to see a distant ball, move closer, reach, grasp and physically lift/hold it?
whole_task_feasibility.owner: the overseer source audit; the builder independent counterreview
whole_task_feasibility.scope: Completed c2 behavior and pending persistent_goal source 2d7718add with package_pg/command_pg.json; no execution or learning-state changes
whole_task_feasibility.verdict: Useful movement-learning foundation, but the current active objective and caregiver ball do not implement the complete requested task. More training of this unchanged setup is not a defensible complete solution.

findings.finding: The selected physical target is a previously experienced whole-body pose, not a tracked ball to acquire.
findings.evidence: D:/UEMA_wt/persistent_goal_20261025/Source/Python/mimo_bridge/lem_model.py:4649,4704; lem/model/physical_goal.py:15,105,132
findings.impact: Recreating a past pose does not automatically move toward the ball when the ball or body is somewhere new.
findings.next_action: Trace/design object-relative goal and success information into the existing learned planner without substituting simulator-only coordinates for perception.

findings.finding: The active physical route forces one 250-ms command; changed commands must predict immediate improvement over the start. The new persistence window keeps a prior goal for 60 model steps (3 seconds), not until task success.
findings.evidence: pending lem_model.py:2455,6997,7011; physical_goal.py:52
findings.impact: Repeated replanning can produce longer locally improving behavior. It does not evaluate an initially worse action for its later benefit, such as planting a hand to move the body before reaching.
findings.next_action: Identify the smallest learned sequence/value connection that scores eventual object acquisition and provides future body state; merely removing the one-step clamp is unsound.

findings.finding: The hand stage fits a remembered finger shape from current joint angles and velocities, rather than scoring object retention through finger contact forces.
findings.evidence: pending lem_model.py:7128; lem/model/hand_response.py:100,112,122
findings.impact: Finger motion and pose following remain useful; they are not a complete learned grasp objective.
findings.next_action: Connect contact-sensitive outcome prediction to selection and learning of hand actions.

findings.finding: The configured crib target is a mocap ball. With toy-hand-off follow, code attaches its motion to the hand after sustained multi-part contact; forces do not lift that ball.
findings.evidence: Source/Python/mimo_bridge/env.py:376,390; caregiver.py:161,428,463; pending command_pg.json:263
findings.impact: Assisted contact/carry experience is retained, but cannot establish a force-supported grasp of a free ball. Separate free boxes exist.
findings.next_action: Specify a free dynamic object and physical lift/retention outcome using existing scene support, preserving assisted scenes as separately labeled experience.

whole_task_feasibility.usable_learning: Keep all eight worlds, learned sensory/body predictors, hand controls, saved command/outcome data and c2 improvement evidence. No reset or claimed percentage of lost training. Assisted carrying is labeled separately from physical grasping.
whole_task_feasibility.counterargument: One-step replanning plus a learned model can generate multi-action behavior where each step makes useful local progress. No claim that all long sequences or spontaneous grasps are mathematically impossible. Current task semantics and mocap-ball dynamics are concrete limitations.
whole_task_feasibility.v4_constraint: v4 addendum lines756/1191/1752 rejects explicit task rewards, a trained task policy and a hidden milestone curriculum. Required connections must support self-selected desired consequences from perception and learned wellness; the external ball-acquisition measurement must not become a scripted crawl/reach/grasp controller or simulator-coordinate teacher.
whole_task_feasibility.alternate_routes_addendum: Verified Oct25 15:52PDT: contact-learning defaults off in pending train_mimo.py:771 and is absent from command_pg.json; ConsequenceLesson is therefore inactive. self-choice is explicitly off. consequence_learning.py:176 revalues recorded moments against current needs; it does not itself select commands using its future predictions. Existing modules are possible reusable pieces, not an active whole-task solution. Source: mailbox/reach-sequence-addendum-20261025/message.json.

one_start_source_reading.text: SOURCE READING of the command differences (overnight-physical-rank-launch-reconciled-20261022; existing source at fd4236974, no load or run). (1) BODY ROWS: the sent order is exec_order -> _canonical_hand_order (gof_probe_harness.py 902-930): under wrist_relative_v1 the finger rows' fields 0:7 are replaced by MuJoCo forward kinematics (hand_target_control.py project_world_orders 316-364 or canonical_from_joints 371-387), their rotations from SciPy Rotation.from_matrix(...).as_quat() (lines 364, 386) with no sign canonicalization; fields 7:9 (radius, strength) and every non-hand row are left as planned (the limb projection is off for this checkpoint: parent_relative_targets off, reach_projection off, env.py 1296-1300). The predicted order's finger rows come from the torch forward kinematics (assemble_world, hand_target_control.py 240). So the 1.44 to 1.67 maxima lie in the finger rows' rotation fields; with positions equal to 3.8e-06 cm, a sign flip (q against -q, the same rotation) fits them (a flip gives twice a component, here 0.72 to 0.84) but is NOT verified: the per-column arrays were not retained (the v3 record keeps only the maximum over fields 3:9 of all body rows; start_0_0.npz holds sensor tokens), so no reconstruction from saved data is possible. A sign flip does not change the world's movement (MuJoCo uses the rotation); it can change the body head's input, which reads the order's raw numbers (efference.py 577) and is trained on the sent (MuJoCo/SciPy) form while planning queries carry the torch form: effect unmeasured. The 0.05 to 0.40 differences are therefore made by the world's eye reflexes, not the model. They can change the head's input eye row between training (issued) and planning (planned); they cannot change the physical score directly (gaze is left out of it). Neither difference is shown to cause the reflex/hold swap or the 3.7 to 6.4 under-prediction; the start's own score before any command is not in the table, so whether hold improves on the start is not shown.
